body_long:
Hôtel Martinez is changing the face it shows the Croisette. The Cannes landmark is removing the rotunda entrance added in 2003 and replacing it with a new Art Deco front, in time for the 80th Cannes Film Festival in May. The works, worth several million euros, were reported on 26 November 2026.

## A new front door

The plan brings a backlit Art Deco canopy, a revolving door and a replanted garden with pergolas. A new veranda will extend Le Sud, the restaurant facing the boulevard. The hotel remains open during the works, and its interiors have been rearranged so that guests see as little of the site as possible.

## A 1930s icon

The Martinez is one of the great hotels of the Croisette, built in the 1930s and known worldwide for its role during the Film Festival. It is run by Hyatt within The Unbound Collection by Hyatt, on behalf of its owner, Constellation Hotels Holdings. Its last major renovation was completed in 2018, and it counts 409 rooms and suites.

## The signal

On the Croisette, the entrance is part of the product. For two weeks a year, the world's cameras film the steps, the canopy and the door. By redesigning exactly what they see, the Martinez treats its façade as a stage, and its arrival experience as a brand asset.

Good luck to the Martinez teams for a smooth season of works.
summary: The Cannes landmark replaces its 2003 rotunda with an Art Deco entrance, canopy and garden, due in May for the 80th Film Festival.
title: Hôtel Martinez gives the Croisette a new Art Deco entrance
why: The Festival's most filmed façade gets a new face.
